title: Hybrid H-tree driving sector buffers that drive global clock grid with tunable deskew
decision: Use a buffered H-tree from central PLL to drive distributed sector buffers which then drive a chip-wide global clock mesh, with programmable delay at sector buffers and local clock buffers regenerating local clocks
rationale: Large ~400mm2 die and SOI process variation make pure balanced tree too skew-sensitive; global grid lowers local skew and allows post-silicon tuning to correct systematic skew while containing insertion delay
outcome: Achieved low global skew enabling >1 GHz target, with tunable delay providing measured deskew range and robust distribution to two cores and caches
weakest_point: Exact terminology sector buffer vs clock sector and whether programmable delay was at sector buffer or earlier tree stage

title: Predominantly static CMOS implementation with restricted selective dynamic circuits
decision: Implement the chip primarily in static CMOS, allowing dynamic Domino only in highly critical datapath macros under strict noise and keeper rules
alternatives_or_rejected: Widespread dynamic Domino logic as used in earlier high-frequency designs
rationale: SOI floating-body increases noise sensitivity, history effect, and leakage concerns; static improves noise margin, LSSD testability, and reduces extensive noise analysis burden
outcome: Met frequency target with manageable noise verification and full LSSD coverage, avoiding SOI-specific dynamic instabilities
weakest_point: Whether paper explicitly frames alternative as widespread Domino or just says limited use of dynamic without naming full dynamic as rejected alternative

title: SOI history effect bounded by early/late timing corners with body-voltage extremes
where_in_paper: Technology - SOI device considerations and Timing methodology
decision: Model SOI threshold variation due to floating-body history by timing every path twice with worst-case body at high and low voltage for late and early modes
rationale: Body potential depends on switching history and cannot be predicted cycle-accurately at static timing time; conservative bounding guarantees operation across all possible histories
outcome: Incorporated into EinsTimer as dual-corner SOI analysis, adding systematic guardband but ensuring hardware works over history variation and parasitic bipolar effects
weakest_point: Specific tool name EinsTimer and exact early/late body voltage polarity mapping could be swapped or belong to companion methodology description

title: Pulsed L1/L2 LSSD latches with local clock choppers for time borrowing
decision: Use IBM L1/L2 LSSD level-sensitive latches driven by locally generated narrow pulses from clock choppers in local clock blocks, permitting limited cycle stealing
alternatives_or_rejected: Edge-triggered flip-flops or traditional non-overlapping two-phase clocks without pulse narrowing
rationale: Reduces latch insertion delay and clocking overhead, improves cycle time, allows absorption of local path variation and imbalance while preserving LSSD scan testability
outcome: Lower latch delay contributed to frequency target, retained full DC scan, enabled controlled time borrowing across critical paths
weakest_point: Direction of decision - whether pulse was on L1 only vs both L1/L2, and exact amount of borrowing allowed
